testing.cli.all_alone: --all runs every test of the game as it is: no test file, --game or --headless with it
testing.cli.after_for_system_tests: --after is for system tests (Ruby tests leave nothing behind)
testing.cli.after_needs_test: --after needs the system test this run goes on from
testing.cli.after_needs_work: --after needs --work: the folder the earlier run kept its files in
testing.cli.game_for_ruby_tests: --game is for Ruby tests (a system test names its game first)
testing.cli.headless_for_system_tests: --headless is for system tests (Ruby tests never open a window)
testing.cli.ruby_without_game: --ruby runs one file of Ruby tests, without a game
testing.cli.usage: redgem-test runs the tests of a game. It is a development tool: built games do not have it.
play the game with a system test at the controls
run a file of Ruby unit tests
run every test of the game (tests/*_test.rb), system tests
with no window; a line per file, PASS or FAIL
--headless            no window: faster, and takes no pictures
--work <dir>          a folder of this run's own for its save file and its notes to the tests
run with it (default: folders every run on this machine shares)
--after <earlier_test.rb>  with --work: go on from that test's run in the same folder, as if
the game were started again (its save, settings and bindings)
--gpu auto|dedicated|integrated      graphics card for this run (default: the saved setting)
--game <game_dir>     the game whose classes the Ruby tests use, from its scripts folder
(default: classes come from the test file's own folder)
It exits with 0 when the tests pass and with 1 when they do not.
testing.cli.work_for_system_tests: --work is for system tests (Ruby tests leave nothing behind)
